issues.legal_issue: A mortgage deed stating that the property becomes an absolute transfer if the debt is not repaid within a fixed period is construed as making the mortgagee the owner when that condition is met, if the stipulation is enforced.
material_facts: The deed secured a loan against a shop and required repayment within 15 years for redemption.

The deed stated that after the 15-year period the shop would be deemed an absolute transfer, and used the words “Mala Kalam,” which the Court understood in context to mean that the mortgagor would have no further say.
The debt was not repaid within the stipulated period.
issues.conclusion: If the deed’s terms were enforced, the mortgagee would become the absolute owner of the shop after the stipulated period expired without repayment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court construed the deed’s words in their context: a term that left the mortgagor no scope to assert any further say over the property meant that the mortgagor lost title and the mortgagee became its absolute owner. This construction addressed the effect of the term if it prevailed; the Court separately held that the term was unenforceable as a clog on the equity of redemption.

predicates.mortgage_redemption_dispute: A party seeks to redeem property given as security for a debt.
predicates.deed_provides_absolute_transfer_after_no: The deed states that the secured property will become an absolute transfer if the debt is not repaid within a fixed period.
predicates.debt_unpaid_when_fixed_period_expired: The borrower or the borrower's successor did not repay the debt before the fixed period expired.

issues.definition: When a redemption dispute involves a deed providing for absolute transfer after nonpayment within a fixed period and the debt remains unpaid at expiry, the mortgagee becomes the absolute owner if the stipulation is enforced.

issues.legal_issue: A court may refuse to enforce a mortgage term that unreasonably restricts redemption even when the governing mortgage statute does not apply, where civil courts apply principles of justice, equity and good conscience and no contrary local rule is established.
material_facts: The suit sought redemption of a transaction treated as a mortgage, and the deed provided that the mortgagee would become the owner if the debt was not repaid within 15 years.
The Court accepted that this term was a clog on the equity of redemption because it extinguished the mortgagor’s right to redeem for failure to repay within the fixed period.
The Transfer of Property Act did not apply in the territory when the mortgage was made or when the stipulated period expired.
The appellant produced no material establishing that local law required enforcement of the term or excluded equitable principles.
The Court noted the consistent application of equitable principles by civil courts in mortgage cases, including in a substantial part of Rajasthan, and relied on Namdeo Lokman Lodhi v. Narmadabai.
issues.conclusion: The equitable principle applied despite the non-application of the Transfer of Property Act; the clog could not bar redemption, subject to the general law of limitation, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Civil courts in India apply justice, equity and good conscience to disputes where no applicable statutory rule governs. In Namdeo Lokman Lodhi v. Narmadabai, the Court stated that courts must apply those principles even when the Transfer of Property Act does not apply. The Court relied on the consistent Indian High Court practice of refusing to enforce unreasonable restraints on redemption, including the approach in Venkata Reddy v. Parvati Ammal, Ramji bin Tukaram v. Chinto Sakharam, Bapuji Apaji v. Sonavaraji Marvadi and Ramasami Sastrigal v. Samiyappanayakan. It distinguished the strict approach in Pattabhiramier v. Vencatarow Naicken and Thumbusawmy Moodelly v. Hossain Rowthen in light of that established judicial practice. It also referred to decisions applying the principle underlying section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act where that Act was not in force.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_proceeding and term_unreasonably_restricts_redemption and no_applicable_mortgage_statute and civil_courts_apply_equity_in_legal_gaps and no_contrary_local_rule_established

predicates.mortgage_redemption_proceeding: A party brings a proceeding to redeem property given as security for a debt.
predicates.term_unreasonably_restricts_redemption: The mortgage term unreasonably restricts the mortgagor’s ability to redeem the property.
predicates.no_applicable_mortgage_statute: No applicable enacted mortgage rule governs the dispute.
predicates.civil_courts_apply_equity_in_legal_gaps: Civil courts apply principles of justice, equity and good conscience when no specific rule governs the dispute.
predicates.no_contrary_local_rule_established: No party establishes a local rule that requires enforcement of the restrictive term or excludes equitable principles.

issues.definition: When a redemption proceeding involves an unreasonable restriction on redemption, no applicable enacted mortgage rule governs, civil courts apply equity in legal gaps, and no contrary local rule is established, the restriction cannot bar redemption.
